doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Branford Marsalis on roots, and backing Oliver Lake
summary: Watkins relays a Branford Marsalis lecture on learning from earlier players, then recalls Oliver Lake who knew no standards but Dolphy tunes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Right. And that’s debatable. And you mentioned to me before Branford Marsalis. I went to a Branford Marsalis lecture a few weeks ago at the University of Pittsburgh. And it was interesting. He pointed out that he has, you know, a student that wants to play like John Coltrane and is just listening only to John Coltrane. And he said, “How do you think he got to play that way? Do you think he sat and listened to albums of his future self and transcribed it?” He said, “You’ve got to listen to the people — who was John Coltrane listening to is the question if you want to learn to play like Trane.” So you know, he’s one of the people that’s a firm believer in you have to have those roots before you move forward and to more modern things. And there’s a lot of different feelings on that you know. I remember being struck when I was a very young man and had the incredible opportunity to play and back up Oliver Lake. And Oliver Lake, we went to get the set list

together and I had no business being on the stage with Oliver Lake but I was thrilled. And we were tasked to put together a set list. He said to us, he said he didn’t know any standards. He didn’t know the American Songbook. He didn’t know things like, just things that you would think a jazz musician would know. But he did know some things like Eric Dolphy tunes and so I don’t think he would be somebody, and I might be wrong about this but I wouldn’t guess he’s somebody that’s versed in twenties and thirties music and the big band music of the mid-twentieth century, and even bebop for that matter. I think his starting point is later. And I can respect that because that’s the reason he plays the way he plays.
I mean that’s the one thing I’ve learned is that there are some rules but, you know, the opinions are wide. I mean there are so many different ways to go about this.
